messages:
Liam: Heads up — since ~02:10 UTC we’re seeing a fleet-wide uptick in GPU recovery events across multiple pools (us-west1 and eu-central). capacity dropped ~6.8% and autoscaler immediately launched replacements, cost jumped unexpectedly. not just soft ECC, also recurring NVLINK parity warnings and occasional Xid 13 logs. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: Automated alert: gpu_recoveries > 250 in 5m across labels: nvlink=true, hw_error_rate>0.7 — alert_id: alert-8932
Maya: rough P95 latency impact on serving? any user-facing errors?
Liam: No hard 5xxs yet, tail latency up ~40ms for some LLM routes. most requests still succeed. but we’re burning spare capacity and hitting burst limits on reserved pools.
Raj: can someone dump last 1h of Node GPU error counts? quick promql I usually run: `sum by (node) (increase(nvidia_gpu_error_count[1h]))`
Sophia: Also check routing fallback thresholds — if capacity dips, traffic routing is bouncey and we’re sending to cheaper region which bumps p50 for EU traffic. Might want a temporary stricter region pin for critical routes.
Jules: I see repeated per-card chatter on rack-07B in us-west1 in the logs. NVLINK resets followed by driver rebinds. suspect a firmware/firm interaction. recommend isolating that rack ASAP to stop churn.
Anika: Cost impact calc: autoscaler added 18 nodes in the last 12 minutes — estimated ~$2.3k/hr incremental if sustained. Notifying finance if we need an emergency cap.
Deckard: Can run a quick ejection on the noisy nodes and force replacing with verified nodes from spare pool. Command I’d run: ```fleetctl --cluster prod drain --nodes rack-07B-* --reason "nvlink-flare" --evacuate```
Liam: Good. @Jules please confirm candidate nodes to drain. @Maya can you flip route pinning for critical models to dedicated-usw1 for the next 30m?
Jules: Confirming nodes: rack-07B-01..07 show error bursts. I’ll tag them `nvlink-flare` and kick the drain now.
Maya: On it — setting route override for route `text-gen-critical` to dedicated-usw1, TTL 30m. Will monitor latency and rollback if p95 > 200ms.
Raj: After draining, please attach the diagnostic bundle: `gpu-diagnostics collect --nodes rack-07B-0{1..7} --out /tmp/rack07b.tgz`. I want the nvlink logs and dmesg before reboots.
Liam: Quick log snippet from rack-07B-03 just before a reboot: `[2026-03-18T02:12:41Z] nvlink: parity error on link 2, resetting bridge` then `Xid 13: GPU fault, context 0x3f`
Anika: Also note: autoscaler policy currently set to aggressive for p99 latency protection. We can throttle scale-outs to avoid cost spikes and accept slightly higher queueing for non-critical routes. Need a decision now.
Sophia: I prefer throttling scale-outs for the next 20m and leaning on route pinning for critical workloads. That limits churn and helps diagnostics.
Jules: Drains started, nodes are entering `cordoned` state. Evacuation progress: 4/7 done.
ops-bot: Deployment note: maintenance window opened by Liam at 02:22 UTC for `rack-07B` — automated host replacement queued.
Liam: Action items: 1) finish draining rack-07B and collect diagnostics (owner: Jules/Raj). 2) hold aggressive autoscaling for 20m (owner: Anika/Maya). 3) cost alert if >$3k/hr sustained (owner: Anika). 4) follow-up healthcheck sweep across all racks with nvlink label (owner: Deckard).
Anika: I’ll also open a temporary billing cap and message finance — copy of alert sent.
Deckard: Will kick a fleet-wide nvlink probe to validate other racks: `nvlink-prober run --filter label=gpumodel=A100 --parallel 20` and post results in 15m.
Maya: If we see firmware correlation across affected nodes, we may need a coordinated firmware rollback. keep that as contingency.
Liam: Good. If anyone sees new Xid storms (100+/5m) escalate to Sev-2. Otherwise we’ll treat this as a mitigation/troubleshoot. Posting diagnostics bundle when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
